narrative: The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 34%. Although that is not a majority, it was above the risk cutoff used for this loan, so your application was denied. The strongest reason was your checking account status: your account is below zero DM, and approved applicants much more often have no overdraft or a positive balance; only about 12.6% of approved cases were below zero. This factor pushed the decision toward bad credit more than any other. The second most influential factor was your installment rate of 2% of disposable income, below the approved average of about 3%, which worked in your favor. The third was your used-car loan purpose, which also slightly reduced the assessed risk. However, those favorable points were not enough to offset the concern raised by the overdrawn account. To improve your chances, focus first on bringing the checking account into positive balance and keeping it there for several months. Ask the bank what account behavior and documentation would make you eligible, consider requesting a smaller amount or a shorter term than the 36 months you requested, and reapply once your account status and savings position have improved.
